topology: R1-R2-R3 form internal AS65000, with full-mesh iBGP peering to Loopback0 10.255.1.1/10.255.2.2/10.255.3.3. OSPF10 carries only internal transits and passive /32 peer loopbacks. R3 peers directly to R4 in AS65100 on172.16.34.0/30. PC1 uses R1 client LAN, PC2 is the independent R2 local control, and SRV1 uses the R4 service LAN. Only R1 originates192.168.10.0/24 and R4 originates192.168.40.0/24 in BGP; no host LAN or external peering subnet is injected into OSPF.
implemented: Twenty-sixth ENARSI Layer 3 Technologies entry with independent practice/reference documents, seven-row addressing/role plan, staged guide, verified ordinary IOS/Windows commands and current-origin/path/query permalinks. Existing themes, icons, terminal styling, layout and offline single-HTML delivery are preserved.

Practice has eight Established directed BGP sessions but R1/R2 receive an inaccessible172.16.34.2 service next hop. The path remains visible with no valid/best flags and is neither installed nor re-advertised. Actual failed probes in both service directions and working PC2/R2 controls earn the initial diagnosis; a session summary alone is insufficient.

R3 next-hop-self toward both internal neighbors changes the received service next hop to its OSPF-reachable10.255.3.3 loopback. R1/R2 install iBGP AD200 paths with AS path65100; R3 installs the external service at AD20. R3 receives the client via iBGP with empty AS path, and R4 receives it externally with AS path65000. Physical data forwarding uses R1-R2-R3-R4 through recursive resolution, not synthetic direct loopback links.

Six observed incidents cover explicit incorrect peering sources on both ends, withdrawn peer-loopback IGP reachability, inaccessible preserved next hop, a missing R1/R3 full-mesh pair, a working R2 route-reflector alternative and service-network withdrawal. Each requires received peer/path/RIB state, three real requests/replies or correlated No route failures in each service direction, both independent working controls and fresh restored full-mesh traffic.

Source exercise deliberately binds both R1/R3 neighbor sources to physical Gi0/1 addresses while expecting peer loopbacks; it does not assume that omitting update-source on only one passive peer always breaks a connection. IGP-withdrawal checks allow actual TCP/hold timeout before asserting failed peers; physical OSPF peers and local controls remain operational.

A plain R1-R2-R3 iBGP chain cannot propagate another iBGP-learned prefix. In the reflector alternative, R2 marks R1/R3 as clients and uses cluster ID2.2.2.2. R1 service path arrives from R2 but preserves next-hop10.255.3.3 and AS path65100, with Originator3.3.3.3 and cluster2.2.2.2; R3 client path has Originator1.1.1.1. Actual ICMP and complete HTTP work in this alternative. Final restoration removes reflection and restores the direct R1/R3 peer.

Fixed BGP runtime/CLI fidelity: policy-accepted inaccessible paths are retained for show ip bgp with inaccessible/no-best state while excluded from selection, installation and advertisement. Reflection ORIGINATOR_ID/CLUSTER_LIST attributes are cleared on eBGP export. Actual iBGP TCP packets now start at TTL255, matching IOS; neighbor output uses configured external hop limits rather than reporting255 for every multihop value.

Seven live checks cover policy, received OSPF underlay, transported peer sessions, received BGP attributes/advertisements, installed recursive routes, HTTP health and saved configs. Nine observations cover diagnosis, four-direction traffic, completed HTTP and six incidents. Practice0/16, diagnosis1/16, repaired baseline10/16, full16/16; reference has only seven live goals. Configuration-only, partial and stale evidence are rejected; YAML retains earned work and rebuilds runtime.
scope: IOS IPv4 unicast iBGP/eBGP within this single internal-AS topology, loopback peering, received logical BGP messages over modeled TCP, recursive next-hop resolution, ordinary split horizon and one route reflector. Native checks cover actual TCP179 denial, real OPEN/KEEPALIVE recovery, exact network origination, wrong remote AS, reset/reload, wire TTL and external attribute stripping. This does not claim a fresh CML capture, complete RFC4271 binary UPDATE encoding, every route-reflector hierarchy/loop case, confederations or complete multiprotocol interoperability.
